main_claim: Contractive differential-equation GNN layers that co-evolve features and adjacency improve GNN robustness to adversarial attacks.
evidence: Theoretical derivation plus numerous real-world benchmarks; on-par or improved performance versus existing methods.
rationale: Title asserts contractive systems improve GNNs; abstract evidence is 'on par or improved', so title is somewhat more certain than results.

main_claim: Adding a pixel-level reconstruction task to pruning improves downstream transfer and outperforms state-of-the-art.
evidence: Empirical study on unnamed benchmark downstream tasks; no numbers reported.
rationale: Title matches evidence; abstract's 'we show image-level pretraining is not capable' for diverse tasks is a sweeping claim without stated support.

main_claim: HumorBench shows STEM reasoning progress transfers effectively to humor comprehension in LLMs.
evidence: About 300 expert-annotated cartoon-caption pairs; benchmarking of current SOTA models.
rationale: Question title is fine; 'transfers effectively'/'strong transferability' infers a transfer mechanism from cross-model benchmark correlations on a small set.

main_claim: Meta-SpikeFormer is a general Transformer SNN with overwhelming advantages, SOTA SNN results across vision tasks.
evidence: 80.0% ImageNet-1K top-1, +3.7% over SOTA SNN; classification, detection, segmentation.
rationale: Title says it inspires next-gen chip design, abstract only discusses this; 'overwhelming advantages' exceeds a 3.7% reported gain.

main_claim: G2PTL, a geography-graph pretrained model for delivery addresses, improves delivery-related logistics tasks.
evidence: Four downstream logistics tasks on real-world data; deployed in Cainiao production; no numbers.
rationale: Claims are scoped to Cainiao logistics tasks; 'significantly improves' lacks numbers but stays within stated setting.

main_claim: Good representations alone are insufficient for sample-efficient RL unless approximation quality passes hard thresholds.
evidence: Lower bounds with sharp thresholds; exponential sample-complexity separations across RL settings.
rationale: Strong statements are backed by stated lower-bound theorems under stated representational conditions; question title answered by abstract.

main_claim: Hyperbolic sphere-packing feature learning (HACK) yields emergent prototypicality enabling superior unsupervised instance selection.
evidence: Qualitative observation that images move toward origin with congealing; no datasets or numbers.
rationale: Claims of superior selection, better generalization and robustness are asserted as demonstrated without any reported evaluation.

main_claim: Generative Model Identification setting and RKME-based solution let users find suitable generative models from one image.
evidence: Single example image gives average top-4 identification accuracy above 80%.
rationale: Title's sufficiency claim 'find the most suitable model' with one image exceeds top-4, ~80% accuracy evidence.

main_claim: Conic Linear Units outperform ReLU across many models and significantly improve diffusion model training.
evidence: Comparisons in MLP, ResNet, UNet and diffusion models; better loss and convergence; no numbers.
rationale: Title credits orthogonal equivariance though gains also involve multi-head/scaling tricks; 'significantly', 'fundamentally changes' unquantified.

main_claim: OmniLayout-1M dataset plus coarse-to-fine 0.5B LLM achieves strong layout generation across domains.
evidence: Six document types in dataset; experiments on multiple domains of M6Doc versus experts and LLMs.
rationale: Title's 'Universal' document layout generation is broader than six document types and one evaluation dataset; abstract claims stay scoped.

main_claim: Task weights affect only the multiplicative factor, not the exponent, of multilingual MT scaling laws.
evidence: Large-scale study of multilingual NMT scaling; in- and out-of-domain test sets, ChrF and BLEURT.
rationale: Findings are scoped, but predicting performance 'with any language weighting at any scale' extrapolates beyond the studied range.

main_claim: Augmented GNNs with skip connections and normalization learn and generalize better, beating message-passing GNNs on hard instances.
evidence: Synthetic hidden-clique datasets with varying difficulty; comparison of GNN architectures.
rationale: 'Learning to solve' read as task description; abstract claims are limited to synthetic hidden-clique instances tested.

main_claim: A single hidden node suffices to reconstruct an input from gradients; mini-batch reconstruction needs units exceeding B.
evidence: Theoretical analysis; validation on fMRI, ECG, cell images, MNIST, CIFAR100, faces.
rationale: Question title; theoretical claims stated with architecture conditions and validated on named data, so no overreach.

main_claim: Negative data augmentation improves GAN generation, anomaly detection and contrastive representation learning.
evidence: Proof under suitable conditions; image generation, anomaly detection, image/video downstream classification, detection, action recognition.
rationale: Claims stated with conditions and multiple tasks; broad generalisation is hedged with 'suggest'.

main_claim: At equal parameter budgets, CNN ensembles can give better accuracy and faster training than single networks.
evidence: Extensive controlled experiments across various architectures and datasets; training time, inference time, memory.
rationale: Claim is qualified ('a wide design space where'), matching the described experimental framework.

main_claim: Benchmark suggests unconstrained-latent models (ViMON, OP3) learn stronger object representations than spatial-transformer models.
evidence: Three datasets, seven test sets; four unsupervised object-centric methods compared.
rationale: Findings explicitly hedged ('suggest', 'may') and limited to four named methods.

main_claim: GD/SGD on two-layer ReLU nets with polylog width reaches epsilon test error with stated sample/iteration counts.
evidence: Theorems with explicit width, sample and iteration bounds; relies on positive kernel separation margin.
rationale: Title sufficiency claim matches the stated theorem for shallow ReLU networks; assumptions are stated.

main_claim: Several popular mutual-information objectives can yield representations insufficient for optimal control under mild assumptions.
evidence: Theoretical sufficiency conditions; deep RL experiments on a simulated visual game.
rationale: Claims hedged ('can yield') and tied to stated assumptions and theory; question title answered.

main_claim: MMTEB, the largest multilingual embedding benchmark to date, plus cheaper downsampled benchmarks preserving rankings.
evidence: Over 500 tasks, 1,000+ languages; evaluation of representative models; downsampled benchmarks.
rationale: Superlative 'largest to date' is quantified and qualified; resource claims match described contents.

main_claim: Heavy-tailed gradient noise is a root cause of SGD underperforming Adam; ACClip outperforms Adam on BERT.
evidence: Empirical and theoretical evidence; convergence analysis under heavy-tailed noise; BERT pretraining and finetuning.
rationale: Causal claim backed by stated empirical and theoretical evidence; title 'Why' slightly more definitive than 'a root cause'.

main_claim: Sage evaluates LLM judges via consistency without human labels; top LLM judges are inconsistent.
evidence: 650 questions; correlation with LLMBar and RewardBench2; top models fail ~25% of hard cases.
rationale: Core claims supported, but 'fine-tuning judges is an unreliable method' and 'situational preference explains' rubric effects are broader than reported evidence.

main_claim: Online meta-critic learning improves off-policy actor-critic methods in continuous control.
evidence: Variety of continuous control environments with DDPG, TD3 and SAC.
rationale: Improvement claim scoped to named base methods and continuous control environments.

main_claim: DataInf approximates influence scores accurately and orders of magnitude faster than existing methods.
evidence: Theory for LoRA; experiments on RoBERTa-large, Llama-2-13B-chat, stable-diffusion-v1.5.
rationale: 'Efficiently' in title supported; abstract claims tied to named models and quantified speedups.

main_claim: GraphGen handles domain, open-set and source-free shifts, outperforming SOTA in source-free open-set DAOD.
evidence: Experiments on unnamed benchmark datasets; no numbers given.
rationale: Title's 'One Graph Can Generalize' implies broad generalisation; abstract reports SOTA on unnamed benchmarks within one task setting.

main_claim: Corr2Cause benchmark shows LLMs perform near random at pure causal inference and finetuning fails to generalize OOD.
evidence: Over 200K samples; seventeen LLMs evaluated; in- versus out-of-distribution finetuning tests.
rationale: Findings backed by reported scale; 'first benchmark' is qualified to pure causal inference skills.

main_claim: SHARCS shared concept space gives explainable multimodal predictions and improves performance over other approaches.
evidence: Unnamed experiments, including missing-modality retrieval and cross-modal explanations; no numbers.
rationale: Claims of being model-agnostic and applicable to any modality types/numbers, advancing trustworthy approaches, go beyond described evidence.

main_claim: Rewarding intra-life novelty (DeepCS) matches SOTA on Montezuma's Revenge and improves several Atari games.
evidence: Montezuma's Revenge, Amidar, Freeway, Gravitar, Tutankham, Seaquest (doubles A2C).
rationale: Title hedged ('Can Improve') and supported by named games; abstract conclusion hedged with 'suggests'.

main_claim: AdaFGL, a new paradigm for structure non-IID federated subgraph learning, achieves SOTA.
evidence: Community split and structure non-IID settings on five benchmark datasets.
rationale: 'New paradigm for general federated data settings' is sweeping relative to SOTA on five datasets in two partition settings.

main_claim: Chain-of-Causal Reasoning improves intent understanding and object localization for 3D intent grounding.
evidence: Extensive experiments on 3D intention grounding and 3D visual grounding tasks; no numbers.
rationale: Title slogan makes no assertion; abstract claim scoped to two named tasks.

main_claim: ASCENSION improves time-series augmentation, beating SOTA DA methods and excelling on all trilemma aspects.
evidence: UCR benchmark, 102 datasets; about 7% average classification accuracy improvement.
rationale: Evidence is classification accuracy for time-series augmentation; 'excelling in all aspects of the trilemma' and general title exceed it.

main_claim: Lambda layers outperform convolution and attention counterparts while being more efficient.
evidence: ImageNet, COCO detection/segmentation; 3.2-4.4x faster than EfficientNets; 86.7% with pseudo-labels.
rationale: 'Significantly outperform' tied to named benchmarks and quantified speed-accuracy results.

main_claim: Neural-PSRL makes posterior sampling practical for continuous control, achieving state-of-the-art results.
evidence: State-of-the-art results on HalfCheetah-v3 and Hopper-v3 only.
rationale: Title claims posterior sampling makes RL sample efficient in general; abstract shows SOTA on two MuJoCo domains.

main_claim: LLMs benefit from graph structure mainly when node text is scarce; performance tracks local homophily.
evidence: Node classification with various prompting methods; rich vs scarce text; leakage and homophily probes.
rationale: Findings scoped to node classification and phrased cautiously (correlational 'related to', 'no substantial evidence').

main_claim: DROP, a non-iterative bi-level offline RL method, matches or beats prior offline RL methods.
evidence: Various unnamed benchmarks; comparable or better performance.
rationale: Performance claim modest, but asserting DROP 'fully answered' the three core questions is more certain than evidence.

main_claim: Forward-only policy-gradient structural pruning of LLMs outperforms SOTA in perplexity and most zero-shot tasks.
evidence: LLaMA, LLaMA-2/3, Vicuna, Mistral; C4, WikiText2; 2.7h, 35GB on one A100.
rationale: Claims qualified ('majority of zero-shot tasks') and tied to named models and datasets.

main_claim: Interventional Dual Attention reduces contextual bias, giving SOTA multi-label classification with lower computation.
evidence: State-of-the-art multi-label classification on MS-COCO and PASCAL-VOC; detection experiments.
rationale: SOTA claim tied to named benchmarks; 'significant improvements' unquantified but not beyond stated scope.

main_claim: syre removes almost all symmetry-induced low-capacity states, which correlates with improved optimization.
evidence: Proofs of two mechanisms; experiments where removal 'correlates well' with improvement when entrapment matters.
rationale: Title prescribes removing symmetries to improve optimization unconditionally; abstract hedges to correlation in cases where entrapment is a concern.

main_claim: Gaussian-mixture prototypes (GMDP) improve KD-based incremental object detection over baselines and SOTA.
evidence: PASCAL VOC and MS-COCO under various settings; no numbers given.
rationale: Stacked unquantified intensifiers ('consistently', 'large margin', 'significantly') exceed what the abstract reports.

main_claim: Standard detectors drop to 30-60% of original performance under corruptions; stylization augmentation substantially increases robustness.
evidence: PASCAL-C, COCO-C, Cityscapes-C benchmarks across corruption types, severities and datasets.
rationale: Claims tied to named benchmarks with numbers; 'comprehensive' is mild resource language.

main_claim: Learning exogenous variable distributions improves causal Bayesian optimization and extends it beyond additive noise models.
evidence: Unnamed diverse datasets and application scenarios; no numbers.
rationale: Vague but modest claim of advantages; generalisation to non-ANM structures is a design property, not overstated.

main_claim: DistillMatch, distilling VFM features for multimodal image matching, outperforms existing algorithms.
evidence: Experiments on unnamed public datasets; no numbers.
rationale: Single scoped performance claim on public datasets; absence of numbers alone is not overreach.

main_claim: SMPE framework maintains multi-dimensional permutation equivariance and outperforms SOTA models.
evidence: Auction design, pseudo-inverse computation, wireless resource allocation; up to 8.4% and 14.4% gains.
rationale: Claims scoped to three named task families with numbers.

main_claim: 3D-GRAND instruction tuning enhances grounding and reduces hallucination in 3D-LLMs.
evidence: 40,087 scenes, 6.2M instructions; 3D-POPE benchmark; scaling effect; early sim-to-real signals.
rationale: Title attributes supported by reported results; sim-to-real hedged as 'early signals'; 'pioneering' is resource language.

main_claim: Diverse-prompt self-ensembles (DIV-SE, IDIV-SE) beat baselines on reasoning benchmarks under fixed budget.
evidence: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 on several reasoning benchmarks; +29.6 points on Blocksworld 4/5.
rationale: Title claims for LLMs generally; abstract tests only GPT-3.5 and GPT-4.

main_claim: Structured LaTeX-style text input enhances MLLM document QA and induces structured attention patterns.
evidence: Systematic analysis of input formats; attention analysis; diverse document types; no numbers.
rationale: Title asserts structured attention itself matters; abstract shows structured input improves performance and co-occurs with structured attention.

main_claim: End-to-end trained modality-based recommenders are competitive with and sometimes exceed ID-based models.
evidence: Rigorous experiments on item recommendation with text and vision modalities; several scenarios.
rationale: Claims qualified ('in some cases', 'imply', 'does not hold well') and match described experiments.

main_claim: Linear probes on CoT activations predict final response safety early, beating text-based monitors.
evidence: Average +13 F1 over best alternatives; across model sizes, families and safety benchmarks.
rationale: Quantified claim with stated generalisation settings; deployment implications hedged with 'suggesting'.

main_claim: Full-batch training with explicit regularization matches SGD; SGD's implicit regularization can be completely replaced.
evidence: CIFAR-10 with modern architectures only.
rationale: General title and 'completely replaced' rest on one dataset, though a single counterexample partly supports 'not necessary'.

main_claim: Concept activation vectors quantify relative importance of user-defined concepts in network predictions.
evidence: Shows CAVs learnable from small example sets; meaningful concepts learned; qualitative insights.
rationale: Abstract mainly descriptive of capabilities without broad performance claims.

main_claim: Past-tense reformulation often jailbreaks refusal-trained LLMs, showing refusal training generalizes poorly.
evidence: Ten named models; GPT-4o attack success rises from 1% to 88% on JailbreakBench.
rationale: Strong finding backed by named models and numbers; broader conclusion hedged ('can be brittle', 'not always').
